name: Danish Refugee Council: programmes (charityevals)
beneficiaries_note: Our build: DRC publishes no spending table by country; its charts give the five largest operations (Ukraine about DKK 445m, Yemen 295m, Sudan 180m, Burkina Faso 145m, Afghanistan 120m) and the four regions' turnover (Asia & Europe about 940m, East Africa & Great Lakes 760m, West Africa & Americas 750m, Middle East & North Africa 650m; Annual Report 2025, p. 49, read from the charts). The rest of each region is a judgment spread over its operations by their size in the report (the six closed in 2025 included); Denmark at its share of programme spending (2.7%).
summary: The Danish Refugee Council (DRC) spent DKK 3.5 billion ($524 million) in 2025, almost all of it government, EU and UN grants, helping 7.5 million refugees, displaced people and their hosts in 28 countries (Ukraine, Yemen, Sudan, Burkina Faso and Afghanistan the largest) and asylum seekers and refugees in Denmark: cash and vouchers for 799,000 people, food security and livelihoods, shelter, water and sanitation, rebuilt public facilities, protection and legal aid, mine clearance and risk education, peacebuilding, site management, 154 expert deployments and the Mixed Migration Centre's research. DRC counts the people each sector reached but publishes neither its spending by sector nor what it handed out as cash, and no controlled evaluation of its own, so every part is built from reach, judged shares of spending and the research on its kind of work, with wide ranges, and counted at half by the shared missing-data slider. It comes to about {{result}} years of healthy life per $1,000 (plausible range {{range}}): cash carries about 60% of the result, food security about 15%, shelter, water and sanitation about 18%, protection, the Standby Roster, infrastructure and mine action the rest. The biggest uncertainties are what share of the spending went to cash and how much of it reached people, and how much of a crisis's excess deaths basic-needs aid averts.

sections.title: Adjustments
sections.explainer: Discounts for weaker evidence, what would have happened anyway, credit shared with others, and delivery falling short. All multiply the outcome.

sections.title: Other outcomes, in this model's unit
sections.explainer: charityevals' standard step for outcomes in more than one unit (docs/normalization.md 2.6): each outcome is counted in its own unit (units of value for income and deaths, WELLBYs for life satisfaction, tonnes of CO₂e, chicken pain days) and put into this model's unit by its unit's conversion over this unit's, which the headline's conversion cancels. So each moves only with its own sliders, exactly as in a model of its own unit. The rows are fixed; don't edit them.

rows.label: Death rate among the people reached during the crisis, without the response
rows.explainer: Judgment 0.02 (0.012-0.04) a person-year: Sphere's emergency threshold is a crude death rate of 1 per 10,000 a day (0.037 a year); DRC's 2025 work ran from acute crises above it (Sudan's Darfur, Gaza) to protracted ones close to the baseline (Burkina Faso, Somalia, South Sudan, the DRC), so the average sits between.

rows.label: Death rate in the same populations before the crisis
rows.explainer: The crude death rates of four of DRC's large crisis operations outside Ukraine (Sudan, Yemen, the DR Congo, South Sudan; UN World Population Prospects via the site's country facts), so only excess deaths count. Ukraine's share is valued as consumption only (no excess deaths, below).

rows.label: Food security: share of the excess deaths the response averts among the people reached
rows.explainer: Judgment 2% (0.5-6%): food, cash for food and livelihood inputs in crises raise consumption, and some excess deaths are from hunger and its diseases, but DRC runs no nutrition treatment or health care, which avert most of a response's deaths.

rows.label: Years of the crisis the response covers per person
rows.explainer: Judgment half a year (3-12 months): distributions and cash usually cover a few months of a lean season or the first months after displacement.

rows.label: Food security: deaths averted per person reached (before adjustments)
rows.explainer: Excess deaths over the time covered, times the share the response averts.

rows.label: Share of the deaths averted that are of children under five
rows.explainer: Judgment 45% (30-60%): in mortality surveys of crises the under-five death rate runs about twice the crude rate, and children under five are 17-20% of these populations, so they are 35-40% of all deaths and more of the excess ones (the family guide's 40-60%). The shared age splits have no crisis split for these countries, and the three shares move the result by about 1%.

rows.label: Of the deaths averted at five or older, share aged 5 to 14
rows.explainer: The relief models' shared figure (@death_ages.crisis_share_5_14_of_over5, {{row:share_5_14_of_over5}}, 10-40%): most deaths over five in crises are of adults.

rows.label: Of the deaths averted at 15 or older, share aged 15 to 49
rows.explainer: Judgment 50% (30-70%); the rest at 50 and over, valued at GiveWell's 50-74 weight.

rows.label: Value of a crisis death averted (units of value)
rows.explainer: The site's one value of a death, by age band, times your value of a life.

rows.label: Food security: illness averted per person reached, in DALYs (before adjustments)
rows.explainer: Judgment 0.0005 DALYs (0-0.002): acute malnutrition and its infections averted among those who don't die, beyond the consumption valued below; small because DRC's food support is a few months of food or cash, not treatment.

rows.label: Share of a branch's spending that reaches people as goods, services or transfers
rows.explainer: Judgment 55% (40-70%): DRC's payroll is 37% of its costs (note 10: DKK 1,281.6m of 3,469.7m), the rest goods, transfers, partners, transport and offices; the branches' own staff (distribution, engineers, trainers) deliver part of the value. NRC's 55% for its 37% payroll share. Used for food security, shelter and infrastructure (cash uses csh_transfer_share).

rows.label: US prices in 2017 relative to 2025

rows.label: US prices in 2024 relative to 2025

rows.label: Food security and livelihoods: share of the international programmes' spending
rows.explainer: Judgment 5.8% (3.6-7.4%): $16.2m × 1.06 × 1.61 of $475.2m. The accounts give no sector split, and DRC's IATI data for 2025 cover about a fifth of the spending. Anchor, sector by sector: DRC's people × the 2025 direct cost per person in the same line in the Norwegian Refugee Council's activity accounts (over its people reached): cash 798,900 × $107 = $85.5m, food security 248,600 × $65 = $16.2m, shelter 293,100 × $72 = $21.2m, WASH 1,205,000 × $16 = $19.3m, infrastructure 179,100 × a judged $100 = $17.9m, protection 1,305,000 × $46 (legal $42 and protection $47, a quarter and three quarters) = $59.9m: $220.0m, × 1.06 for NRC's project support (NOK 470.6m on 7,934.7m, which DRC's project costs include) = $233.2m. The sectors with no NRC line are carved out first: the Standby Roster's 'over EUR 7 million in turnover' ($7.9m), mine action in 11 countries (judged $60m: one of the largest humanitarian demining operators, Ukraine its largest), site management (1.7 million residents at a judged $10 = $17m), peacebuilding (45,300 at a judged $100 = $4.5m) and the Mixed Migration Centre (judged $10m): $99.4m. The anchored sectors share the remaining $375.8m of the $475.2m in proportion, 1.61 times their NRC-cost sum. The range runs from no scale-up beyond NRC's costs and project support (low) to full pro rata of all $475.2m over the anchored sectors (high).

rows.label: Food security: value delivered per person (US$)
rows.explainer: The branch's spending that reaches people as food, inputs, grants and training, per person; about $60.

rows.label: PPP conversion (2017 international $ per US $), NRC's African crises
rows.explainer: Three of DRC's African crisis operations (Sudan, the DR Congo, South Sudan; World Bank, via the site's country facts); Yemen and Afghanistan, also large for DRC, have no PPP factor in the site's facts.

rows.label: Consumption per person per year of the people reached in low-income crises (2017 PPP $)

rows.label: Food security: ln(consumption) gain per person
rows.formula: years_exposed * ln(1 + value_delivered_per_person * cpi_2017_vs_2025 * ppp_factor / (baseline_consumption * years_exposed))
rows.explainer: The template's form: goods used up over the months they cover (years_exposed) raise consumption only in those months, so the gain is t × ln(1 + v ÷ (b × t)).

rows.label: Market spillovers of cash and food security, as a share of the recipients' gain
rows.explainer: A side effect: cash and inputs spent in local markets raise traders' and producers' incomes, and savings groups and business grants (3,100 refugee entrepreneurs supported in Kenya, p. 27) employ others; food bought in thin markets can also raise prices for others. The shared figure for cash spent locally, +{{row:market_spillover_share}} (0 to +40%); applied to cash and food security.

rows.label: Consumption per person per year of displaced people in Ukraine (2024 US$)
rows.explainer: Ukraine's household consumption per person from the national accounts, put on the household-survey scale by the site's shared ratio, times the recipients' share of the average.

rows.label: Cash: transfer per person (US$)
rows.explainer: About $92 a person in 2025 dollars.

rows.label: Cash: share of the money transferred in middle-income countries (valued at Ukraine's recipients' consumption)
rows.explainer: Judgment 43% (30-60%): Ukraine, DRC's largest operation (turnover chart, p. 49), runs large multi-purpose cash programmes (a judged 30%), and Lebanon, Iraq, Jordan, Türkiye, Colombia, Venezuela, Libya and Tunisia, about an eighth of DRC's spending, add their cash; Yemen, Sudan, Afghanistan, Syria, Somalia and the Sahel the rest. Valued at Ukraine's recipients' consumption as the stand-in, as shelter's shl_mic_share; these settings take no crisis excess deaths.

rows.explainer: Each group's log gain at its own consumption over the months the transfers cover (years_exposed: the template's t × ln(1 + v ÷ (b × t))), weighted by its share of the money, taken as its share of the people.

rows.label: Shelter: value to households of in-kind shelter as a share of its cost
rows.explainer: The shared figure for housing and shelter given in kind (@aid_value.inkind_housing_vs_cash, 0.8, 0.6-0.95): households can't choose what they get and kits may not match needs; rental cash and repairs are worth close to their cost.

NRC's 30%.

rows.label: Shelter: ln(consumption) gain per person over the years of use
rows.formula: pv_annuity_due(1, $discount_rate, shl_years) * (shl_mic_share * ln(1 + shl_value_per_person / shl_years * cpi_2024_vs_2025 / ukr_consumption) + (1 - shl_mic_share) * ln(1 + shl_value_per_person / shl_years * cpi_2017_vs_2025 * ppp_factor / baseline_consumption))
rows.explainer: The value spread over its years of use, each year's log gain at the group's consumption, discounted at the shared rate.

rows.label: Shelter: share of the excess deaths the shelter averts among the people reached
rows.explainer: Judgment 1% (0.2-4%): no study measures what emergency shelter does to mortality (Maynard, Parker and Twigg 2017, Humanitarian Evidence Programme, rate the health evidence as limited); shelter, insulation and fuel protect against exposure in winter (Afghanistan, Ukraine, Syria).

rows.label: Shelter: deaths averted per person reached (before adjustments)
rows.explainer: Excess deaths over the time covered, times the share averted, in the low-income crises only.

rows.label: Shelter: episodes of acute illness averted per person reached
rows.explainer: The shared figure for shelter, blankets and site work (@humanitarian_response.shelter_illness_episodes_averted, 0.03, 0-0.1).

rows.label: Length of an episode of acute illness
rows.explainer: The shared length of an acute illness episode (@humanitarian_response.acute_illness_episode_years): about five days, three to eleven.

rows.label: Shelter: illness averted per person, in DALYs (before adjustments)
rows.explainer: Episodes × their length × GBD's disability weight for a moderate acute infection.

rows.label: Infrastructure: share of the international programmes' spending
rows.explainer: Judgment 6.4% (3-10%): rehabilitated hospitals, schools, water and energy systems cost more per person served than household aid; at a judged $100 a person, $17.9m × 1.06 × 1.61 of $475.2m; the range is wider than the others' because the cost per person is itself judged. The accounts give no sector split, and DRC's IATI data for 2025 cover about a fifth of the spending. Anchor, sector by sector: DRC's people × the 2025 direct cost per person in the same line in the Norwegian Refugee Council's activity accounts (over its people reached): cash 798,900 × $107 = $85.5m, food security 248,600 × $65 = $16.2m, shelter 293,100 × $72 = $21.2m, WASH 1,205,000 × $16 = $19.3m, infrastructure 179,100 × a judged $100 = $17.9m, protection 1,305,000 × $46 (legal $42 and protection $47, a quarter and three quarters) = $59.9m: $220.0m, × 1.06 for NRC's project support (NOK 470.6m on 7,934.7m, which DRC's project costs include) = $233.2m. The sectors with no NRC line are carved out first: the Standby Roster's 'over EUR 7 million in turnover' ($7.9m), mine action in 11 countries (judged $60m: one of the largest humanitarian demining operators, Ukraine its largest), site management (1.7 million residents at a judged $10 = $17m), peacebuilding (45,300 at a judged $100 = $4.5m) and the Mixed Migration Centre (judged $10m): $99.4m. The anchored sectors share the remaining $375.8m of the $475.2m in proportion, 1.61 times their NRC-cost sum. The range runs from no scale-up beyond NRC's costs and project support (low) to full pro rata of all $475.2m over the anchored sectors (high).

rows.label: Infrastructure: years the rehabilitated facilities serve
rows.explainer: Judgment 5 years (2-10): repaired buildings and water and energy systems last a decade or more, but in active war zones (Mykolaiv, Kharkiv, Sumy) some are damaged again and populations move.

rows.label: Infrastructure: value delivered per person served (US$)
rows.explainer: The works reaching people, valued as goods in kind (the shelter branch's equivalence: people can't choose them).

rows.label: Infrastructure: ln(consumption) gain per person over the years of use
rows.formula: pv_annuity_due(1, $discount_rate, inf_years) * ln(1 + inf_value_per_person / inf_years * cpi_2024_vs_2025 / ukr_consumption)
rows.explainer: The value spread over the facilities' years, each year's log gain at Ukraine's recipients' consumption (most of the work is in Ukraine; elsewhere it would count more), discounted at the shared rate.

rows.label: WASH: diarrhoeal deaths per person-year in the crisis sites
rows.explainer: The shared figure for crisis sites (@humanitarian_response.wash_crisis_diarrhoea_deaths_per_person_year, 0.0008, 0.0004-0.002); DRC's WASH work is concentrated in Sudan, Yemen, Somalia and Gaza, where it runs high, and Ukraine and Lebanon, where it runs low.

rows.label: WASH: fall in diarrhoeal deaths among the people served
rows.explainer: The shared figure for emergency WASH (@humanitarian_response.wash_crisis_diarrhoea_death_reduction, {{row:wsh_diarrhoea_reduction}}, 3-35%).

rows.label: Other deaths averted per diarrhoeal death averted
rows.explainer: GiveWell's shared ratio for water treatment: deaths from other causes that diarrhoea makes more likely.

rows.label: WASH: years the service lasts per person reached
rows.explainer: Judgment a year (6 months to 3 years): water trucking and hygiene kits last months, repaired systems and latrines years.

rows.label: WASH: years of service, discounted
rows.explainer: Each year's benefit at the shared discount rate.

rows.label: WASH: value of a diarrhoeal death averted
rows.explainer: The site's age split of diarrhoeal deaths in Sub-Saharan Africa (facts/death_ages.json, WHO GHE) by the site's values by age.

rows.label: WASH: deaths averted per person served (before adjustments)
WASH: diarrhoea episodes averted per person-year of service
rows.explainer: The shared figure for emergency WASH (@humanitarian_response.wash_crisis_diarrhoea_episodes_averted, 0.1, 0.02-0.3).

rows.label: WASH: diarrhoea illness averted per person, in DALYs (before adjustments)
rows.explainer: Episodes averted × their length × GBD's disability weight for moderate diarrhoea.

rows.label: WASH: value of water-fetching time saved, as a share of consumption
rows.explainer: The shared figure for time saved fetching water, mostly women's and girls' (@water.time_saved_consumption_share, {{row:wsh_time_saved_share}} of consumption, 0-3%).

rows.label: WASH: ln(consumption) gain per person from time saved
Protection: share of participants in legal aid
rows.explainer: Judgment 25% (10-40%): legal aid is one of protection's six sub-sectors (p. 13) and DRC expanded it in 2025 (civil documentation, housing, land and property, legal stay; p. 21); community-based protection, child protection, gender-based violence and psychosocial support reach the rest. NRC's legal assistance was two thirds of its protection participants as a separate core competence.

rows.label: Legal assistance: share of participants counselled or assisted on a legal problem
rows.explainer: The shared figure for displacement legal aid (@humanitarian_response.legal_aid_case_share, {{row:icl_case_share}}, 15-50%): many get legal information in group sessions, the rest individual counselling, assistance or representation.

rows.label: Legal assistance: share of those cases resolved (document, legal stay, tenure secured)
rows.explainer: Judgment 50% (30-70%): no outcome rate across countries; documentation cases usually succeed, housing, land and property and legal-stay cases often stall.

rows.label: Legal assistance: consumption gain for a resolved case
rows.explainer: The shared figure for a resolved legal case (@humanitarian_response.legal_aid_consumption_gain, {{row:icl_consumption_gain}}, 1-15%).

rows.label: Legal assistance: years the gain lasts
rows.explainer: The shared figure (@humanitarian_response.legal_aid_years, 3 years, 1-6).

rows.label: Legal assistance: ln(consumption) gain per participant, discounted
rows.formula: icl_case_share * icl_resolved_share * ln(1 + icl_consumption_gain) * pv_annuity_due(1, $discount_rate, icl_years)
rows.explainer: Only resolved cases count; information alone is counted at nothing here (its value is in unmodelled_benefits_adj).

rows.label: Share of people in conflict-affected populations with a mental disorder
rows.explainer: The shared WHO prevalence in conflict-affected populations (@humanitarian_response.conflict_mental_disorder_prevalence, 22.1%, 18.8-25.7%); DRC's protection participants, survivors and peacebuilding participants are displaced by or living through conflict.

rows.label: Average share of an initial gain kept over its years when it fades linearly to nothing
rows.explainer: A gain that falls in a straight line from its first size to zero averages half its first size over those years.

rows.label: Protection: improvement in mental health for participants with a disorder (SD)
rows.explainer: The shared figure for broad protection work (@humanitarian_response.protection_mental_health_effect_sd, 0.2 SD, 0.05-0.4): DRC's protection beyond legal aid is mostly community-based protection, protection monitoring and referral, with case management, gender-based violence response and psychosocial support for fewer.

rows.label: Protection: years the gain lasts
rows.explainer: Judgment a year (6 months to 2 years), fading linearly; as Save the Children's protection branch.

rows.label: Protection: WELLBYs per participant
rows.explainer: Participants with a disorder × the gain in SD × its years, fading linearly (linear_fade_share), × the shared WELLBYs per SD-year. Participants without a disorder, and violence averted, are in unmodelled_benefits_adj. Also used for mine victims' assistance.

rows.label: Mine action: yearly casualties on a square kilometre of land before release
rows.explainer: Judgment 0.3 (0.05-1.5) a year: Landmine Monitor records about 6,000 casualties of mines and explosive remnants a year worldwide (most civilians) on suspected areas of the order of 100,000 km² or more (Ukraine alone surveys well over 100,000 km²), which averages a few hundredths per km² a year; land put forward for release is chosen for use (farmland, return villages, infrastructure) where most incidents happen, while some of it is cancelled by survey with no hazard found. So between the average and high-impact areas.

rows.label: Mine action: years the release brings safety forward
rows.explainer: Judgment 5 years (2-10): without DRC the land would be cleared later by other operators or national authorities (Ukraine's national programme and a dozen international operators), or people would learn to avoid it; in Yemen, Sudan and Libya clearance capacity is far below the contamination.

rows.label: Mine action: years counted, discounted
rows.explainer: Each year's averted casualties and land use at the shared discount rate.

rows.label: Mine action: yearly chance an item removed in a spot task would have caused a casualty
rows.explainer: Judgment 0.05% a year (0.01-0.2%): the items are reported near homes, farms and roads, where people handle or strike them; most unexploded ordnance lies for years without harming anyone. Anchor: about a fifth of the world's casualties come from such remnants rather than minefields, against millions of items in the ground.

rows.label: Mine action: yearly casualty risk of a person in a contaminated community
rows.explainer: Judgment 3 in 100,000 a year (1-10): Ukraine's few hundred civilian casualties a year among the several million people in contaminated oblasts, and similar rates in Yemen's and Afghanistan's affected districts.

rows.label: Mine action: share of that risk removed for a year by risk education
rows.explainer: Judgment 10% (2-30%): risk education changes what people say they would do, but evaluations rarely measure casualties; most casualties are people who knew the risk and had to use the land (farmers, scrap collectors). A year's effect.

rows.label: Mine action: casualties averted (before adjustments)
rows.formula: mna_land_m2 / 1e6 * mna_casualties_per_km2_year * mna_years_pv + mna_items * mna_item_risk_year * mna_years_pv + mna_eore_people * mna_eore_risk * mna_eore_reduction
rows.explainer: Land released, items removed and risk education, each its own channel; land release is valued from the area, so a hazard that was both cleared and reported is counted once on each path only if it was a spot task outside the released areas, as the report counts them.

rows.label: Mine action: share of casualties killed
rows.explainer: Judgment 30% (25-40%): about a third of the casualties Landmine Monitor records each year are killed, the rest injured.

rows.label: Mine action: share of the deaths that are children
rows.explainer: Judgment 35% (20-50%): children are over a third of civilian casualties where the age is known (Landmine Monitor), most of them boys of 5-14; the rest are valued as adults of 15-49.

rows.label: Mine action: value of a death averted (units of value)
rows.explainer: The site's one value of a death by age band, times your value of a life.

rows.label: Mine action: lasting disability weight of a survivor
rows.explainer: Judgment 0.05 (0.02-0.12): about half of survivors lose a limb; the Global Burden of Disease weighs a leg amputation at about 0.02 long term with treatment (prosthesis) and about 0.16 without, and blindness, hearing loss and other injuries in between; many survivors in these countries have little rehabilitation.

rows.label: Mine action: years a survivor lives with the injury
rows.explainer: Judgment 40 years (25-50): most casualties are children and working-age adults.

rows.label: Mine action: healthy years lost per injury averted
rows.explainer: The disability weight over the survivor's remaining years, discounted at the shared rate.

rows.label: Mine action: people who use a square kilometre of released land
rows.explainer: Judgment 100 (30-300): a square kilometre is 100 hectares, farmland for 20-50 households in Ukraine's and Afghanistan's farming areas, more for village land and roads, less for remote land.

rows.label: Mine action: users' consumption gain from released land, per year
rows.explainer: Judgment 5% (1-15%): land back in production adds a harvest or grazing to a household's other income; much released land was cancelled by survey and partly in use already.

rows.label: Mine action: people using the released land
rows.explainer: Area in km² × users per km².

rows.label: Mine action: ln(consumption) gain per land user over the years counted
rows.explainer: The yearly gain over the years the release brings forward, discounted.

rows.label: Peacebuilding: wellbeing gain of a participant, in SD
rows.explainer: Judgment 0.05 SD (0-0.15): randomised evaluations of community dialogue, mediation and conflict-management training find small and mixed effects on trust and local violence (e.g. Blattman, Hartman and Blair 2014 on mass alternative-dispute-resolution education in Liberia: fewer violent land disputes, some more tension); a quarter of the protection branch's 0.2 SD for people with a disorder.

rows.label: Peacebuilding: years the gain lasts
rows.explainer: Judgment a year (6 months to 3 years), fading linearly; agreements over land and water can last longer, but conflicts move on.

rows.label: Peacebuilding: WELLBYs per participant
rows.explainer: The gain in SD × its years, fading linearly, × the shared WELLBYs per SD-year.

rows.label: Value of a dollar of the humanitarian work improved, as a multiple of cash
rows.explainer: The site's shared value of a dollar of humanitarian aid whose use isn't known more exactly (facts/aid_value.json): about a fifth of cash (0.05-0.8), what the site's relief models say relief does per dollar before their missing-data step, which these branches apply themselves; as NRC's NORCAP. Used for site management, the Standby Roster and the Mixed Migration Centre.

rows.label: Value of a dollar of the humanitarian work improved (units of value)
Site management: aid others deliver per site resident per year (US$)
rows.explainer: Judgment $60 a year ($20-200): the 2025 global appeal sought about $250 a person targeted and got about a third of it; people in managed sites get food, water, health care and shelter from several agencies, but Darfur's and Gaza's sites were badly underserved.

rows.label: Site management: improvement in the value of that aid
rows.explainer: Judgment 3% (0.5-10%): site managers map who lives where, flag gaps and duplication, run feedback and refer protection cases, so the same aid reaches the people most in need; below the 5% for an expert secondee (NRC's NORCAP), because much of the aid would reach residents anyway.

rows.label: Site management: units of value per resident
Standby Roster: programme budget a deployment's work shapes in the year (US$)
rows.explainer: Judgment $0.9m ($0.25m-4m): NRC's NORCAP takes $2m ($0.5m-8m) for an assignment costing about $112,000; the roster's turnover of over EUR 7m over 154 deployments is about $51,000 each, so DRC's deployments are shorter or lighter and shape less in the year, scaled by the cost ratio. A protection, resettlement or cash expert in a UN country office shapes a response of tens of millions shared with many staff.

rows.label: Standby Roster: improvement in the value of that budget
rows.explainer: Judgment 5% (1-15%), as NRC's NORCAP: better targeting, coordination and technical quality, diluted across a whole response. The 4,600 refugees helped to resettlement (p. 35) are part of this.

rows.label: Standby Roster: units of value per deployment
Mixed Migration Centre: yearly migration programming and policy its research informs (US$)
rows.explainer: Judgment $20m ($5m-100m): the centre's 4Mi surveys of people on the move and its regional reports are used by the EU, UNHCR, IOM and NGOs designing protection along the routes to Europe, through North Africa and in Asia and Latin America; a small part of the money spent on migration responses would be shaped by any one source.

rows.label: Mixed Migration Centre: improvement in the value of what it informs
rows.explainer: Judgment 1% (0.2-5%): research informs decisions that many other sources also feed; below the Standby Roster's 5% for an expert inside the response.

rows.label: Mixed Migration Centre: units of value a year (before adjustments)
Denmark: share of legal-service users given individual counselling or representation
rows.explainer: Judgment 40% (20-60%): the 8,796 include people given legal information at asylum centres; the report lists counselling, assistance and representation (208 Dublin appeals, 107 manifestly-unfounded cases, 1,096 return-counselling sessions).

rows.label: Denmark: share of those whose asylum, transfer or return outcome changes because of DRC
rows.explainer: Judgment 2% (0.5-6%): most cases would end the same with the state-appointed lawyer the Refugee Appeals Board provides; DRC's role matters most in Dublin appeals and the manifestly-unfounded procedure, where it is the only adviser, and in choices about voluntary return.

rows.label: Denmark: life-satisfaction gain of protection over transfer or return, per year
rows.explainer: Judgment 1.5 points (0.5-3) on the 0-10 scale: refugees resettled in rich countries report life satisfaction a point or two above people in the conflict countries they fled (Gallup World Poll averages), and a forced return or transfer adds insecurity.

rows.label: Denmark: years the changed outcome lasts
rows.explainer: Judgment 10 years (3-20): protection status is reviewed and may end (Syrians' statuses were reviewed in 2025), and some would later win it by another route.

rows.label: Denmark: WELLBYs per legal-service user
rows.explainer: The share whose outcome changes × the yearly gain over its years, discounted.

rows.label: Denmark: WELLBYs per participant in integration work
rows.explainer: Judgment 0.05 WELLBYs (0.01-0.2): mentoring, homework cafes and network families are light-touch; employment programmes move a few in a hundred into work sooner (Danish randomised trials of active labour-market programmes find effects of a few points), a job worth about half a point of life satisfaction a year.

rows.label: Denmark: value of volunteers' unpaid work, 2025 (euros)

source.title: Danish Refugee Council, Annual Report 2025 (management review and the financial statements for 1 January - 31 December 2025, audited by Deloitte, signed 19 May 2026)
source.quote: it totalled over EUR 5 million in 2025

rows.explainer: DRC's own valuation of its 4,350 volunteers' 400,200 hours ('2 hours a week for 46 weeks'); used for the Denmark branch's share of the resources (Convention 2).

rows.label: Evidence adjustment, food security
rows.explainer: Judgment 0.75 (0.5-1): the death share is a judgment without a trial, and part of the value (seeds, livestock, business grants) depends on harvests and markets.

rows.label: Counterfactual adjustment, food security
rows.explainer: Judgment 70% (45-90%): only 35% of the 2025 appeals' requirements were met, the largest shortfall in appeal history (ALNAP 2026), so others rarely fill the gap a responder leaves; in better-funded places more would have come anyway.

rows.label: Evidence adjustment, cash
rows.explainer: Judgment 0.9 (0.7-1): cash is valued at what recipients get, which trials of cash transfers support well (spent mostly on food and essentials, no rise in temptation goods); some doubt about transfers in fast-moving crises reaching who they should.

rows.label: Counterfactual adjustment, cash
rows.explainer: Judgment 70% (45-90%): only 35% of the 2025 appeals' requirements were met, the largest shortfall in appeal history (ALNAP 2026), so others rarely fill the gap a responder leaves; in better-funded places more would have come anyway. As food security.

rows.label: Evidence adjustment, shelter
rows.explainer: Judgment 0.75 (0.5-1): the value of shelter is its cost to the household, but the health effects are judgments without trials (Maynard et al. 2017).

rows.label: Counterfactual adjustment, shelter
rows.explainer: Judgment 70% (45-90%): only 35% of the 2025 appeals' requirements were met, the largest shortfall in appeal history (ALNAP 2026), so others rarely fill the gap a responder leaves; in better-funded places more would have come anyway. As food security.

rows.label: Evidence adjustment, infrastructure
rows.explainer: Judgment 0.6 (0.3-1): the value of rehabilitated facilities is their cost spread over people served, not a measured benefit; services may lack staff or supplies once rebuilt.

rows.label: Counterfactual adjustment, infrastructure
rows.explainer: Judgment 60% (35-85%): Ukraine's recovery attracts government, World Bank and EU reconstruction money that would rebuild some facilities later; less elsewhere.

rows.label: Evidence adjustment, WASH
rows.explainer: Judgment 0.65 (0.4-1): the fall in deaths rests on meta-analyses of household water and sanitation trials, not on emergency delivery, and on a judged crisis death rate.

rows.label: Counterfactual adjustment, WASH
rows.explainer: Judgment 70% (45-90%): only 35% of the 2025 appeals' requirements were met, the largest shortfall in appeal history (ALNAP 2026), so others rarely fill the gap a responder leaves; in better-funded places more would have come anyway. As food security.

rows.label: Evidence adjustment, protection
rows.explainer: Judgment 0.55 (0.3-0.9): legal aid's income effect is unmeasured (NRC's legal branch 0.5) and protection's wellbeing effect is a judgment from more focused psychosocial trials (NRC's protection 0.6); weighted by the branch's two parts.

rows.label: Counterfactual adjustment, protection
rows.explainer: Judgment 85% (60-100%): few others give displaced people legal aid or protection services in these places; some would get help through UNHCR's other partners. As NRC's legal and protection branches.

rows.label: Evidence adjustment, mine action
rows.explainer: Judgment 0.5 (0.25-0.9): casualty rates on released land, item risks and risk education's effect are judgments with no study of DRC's work; mine action's own evaluations count area and items, not casualties averted.

rows.label: Counterfactual adjustment, mine action
rows.explainer: Judgment 80% (50-100%): the years brought forward already count when others would have cleared the land; this is the share of tasks others would have taken in DRC's place in the same year (operators are few in Yemen, Sudan and Libya, more in Ukraine).

rows.label: Evidence adjustment, peacebuilding
rows.explainer: Judgment 0.5 (0.2-0.9): trials of community peacebuilding are few and mixed, and the effect is a judgment.

rows.label: Counterfactual adjustment, peacebuilding
rows.explainer: Judgment 85% (60-100%): few others run local mediation in these places.

rows.label: Evidence adjustment, site management
rows.explainer: Judgment 0.5 (0.2-0.9): aid per resident and site management's effect on it are judgments; no evaluation compares managed and unmanaged sites.

rows.label: Counterfactual adjustment, site management
rows.explainer: Judgment 60% (30-90%): the camp-coordination cluster assigns site managers; without DRC another agency or the authorities would manage some sites, often later or less well.

rows.label: Evidence adjustment, Standby Roster
rows.explainer: Judgment 0.6 (0.3-1): the budget and improvement are judgments; secondees' value is reported by the hosts, not measured. As NRC's NORCAP.

rows.label: Counterfactual adjustment, Standby Roster
rows.explainer: Judgment 50% (20-80%): host agencies would fill some posts themselves or through other standby partners' rosters, often later or with less experienced staff. As NRC's NORCAP.

rows.label: Evidence adjustment, Mixed Migration Centre
rows.explainer: Judgment 0.5 (0.2-0.9): research use is hard to trace; the budget informed and its improvement are judgments.

rows.label: Counterfactual adjustment, Mixed Migration Centre
rows.explainer: Judgment 60% (30-90%): IOM's displacement tracking, UNHCR and academic research cover some of the same ground; the 4Mi surveys of people on the move are largely unique.

rows.label: Evidence adjustment, Denmark
rows.explainer: Judgment 0.5 (0.3-0.9): no study measures what NGO legal counselling changes in Danish asylum outcomes, or what light-touch integration work does to wellbeing.

rows.label: Counterfactual adjustment, Denmark
rows.explainer: Judgment 70% (40-90%): Danish law gives asylum seekers a state-appointed lawyer before the Refugee Appeals Board and municipalities run integration programmes, so part of DRC's work would be done by others.

rows.label: DRC's share of the resources behind the relief and mine-action outcomes
rows.explainer: Judgment 90% (75-100%): DRC delivers most work itself with its donors' money, which is in its accounts (UN agencies' grants included); it worked with 204 local partners (p. 37), whose grants are DRC's spending, and communities add labour and some goods in kind.

rows.label: Share of credit used, relief branches
rows.explainer: DRC's share of the resources behind the outcome; it applies whichever way credit is shared.

rows.label: DRC's share of the resources, protection
rows.explainer: Judgment 85% (60-100%): authorities issue documents and decide cases, and communities' own time goes into community-based protection; DRC's staff and partners do the rest.

rows.label: DRC's share of the resources, peacebuilding
rows.explainer: Judgment 70% (40-90%): local leaders, committees and authorities give their time to mediation and agreements.

rows.label: DRC's share of the resources, site management
rows.explainer: Judgment 50% (25-80%): the aid improved is others'; DRC adds the coordination, the camp committees and the other agencies' staff do much of the work.

rows.label: DRC's share of the resources, Standby Roster
rows.explainer: Judgment 60% (30-90%): the improvement is made by the host's team and budget with the expert; DRC pays the expert. As NRC's NORCAP.

rows.label: This charity's share of the good done with money, work or budgets it brings in
rows.explainer: The site's one setting for resources another party commits only because of the organisation (docs/normalization.md 2.24): governments' budgets and enforcement, companies' compliance, the use others make of research. The charity is credited this share of the good done with them, net of their cost; the rest stays with those who paid or did the work. Fixed.

rows.label: DRC's share of the work behind the research, Mixed Migration Centre
rows.explainer: DRC's share among those who produce the research: the centre is part of DRC, and some of its work is done with partners (our judgment of their part). The agencies and donors that use the research in their own programmes are under the mobiliser's share, not here. Judgment 90% (70-100%).

rows.label: Share of credit used, Mixed Migration Centre
rows.explainer: The share among those who paid for or did the same work, times the mobiliser's share: the rest of the credit stays with those who carry out or adopt the result (docs/normalization.md 2.24).

rows.label: Denmark: value of volunteers' unpaid work (US$)
rows.explainer: Euros at the IRS's 2025 yearly average.

rows.label: DRC's share of the resources, Denmark
rows.explainer: DRC's own spending on the work in Denmark over it plus its volunteers' unpaid hours at DRC's own valuation (Convention 2): about 70%. Volunteers' unpaid time is the in-kind resource that applies whichever way credit is shared.

rows.label: Share of the reported reach that got the support as modelled
rows.explainer: Judgment 85% (70-95%), every branch: the reach is DRC's own count, rounded and with donors' audits and third-party monitoring of many projects (76% of people surveyed fully satisfied, p. 11); some participants are counted twice within a sector or get only a light touch, and some aid is delayed, diverted or lost in conflict (Sudan, Gaza, Yemen, Myanmar). In 2025 the US stop-work order interrupted projects mid-way (p. 49).

rows.label: Leverage and funging
rows.explainer: 1 (0.85-1.1): 96.5% of DRC's income is restricted grants from governments, the EU and the UN (financial highlights, p. 50); a private gift (2%) co-funds grants, starts responses before grants arrive (the Emergency Reserve Fund) and pays for what grants don't cover, and can't be told apart from them. No sign it pulls in more or is displaced.

rows.label: Missing-data discount, food security
rows.explainer: Thin: people reached is DRC's count, but the branch's spending is a judged share and the deaths averted and value delivered are judgments with no trial of DRC's work. So it is counted less by the shared slider, the same way in every model (docs/normalization.md 2.12).

rows.label: Missing-data discount, cash
rows.explainer: Thin: DRC counts the people who got cash but publishes neither the branch's spending nor the money transferred, so the transfer per person is a judgment. So it is counted less by the shared slider, the same way in every model (docs/normalization.md 2.12).

rows.label: Missing-data discount, shelter
